Every study follows the same arc

No matter the passage, each study moves through the same ten stops — once you know the shape, you always know where you are in it.

  1. 1
    AnchorOne sentence to read first and return to throughout — the whole study orbits it.
  2. 2
    The TextThe passage itself, printed in full — NASB 1995 and ESV side by side, never silently substituted.
  3. 3
    Where This SitsThe passage in its context — what comes before it, what it's answering, what turns on it.
  4. 4
    The Movement of ThoughtHow the passage actually argues, verse by verse, laid out as a single line of reasoning.
  5. 5
    The Neuroplasticity BridgeA modest, text-grounded note on repetition and the renewing of the mind — tied to the passage and the Spirit's work, never dressed up as self-help.
  6. 6
    AuDHD ReframeWhere the text speaks directly to an Autistic or ADHD experience — only where the text actually supports it.
  7. 7
    Words That Carry WeightThe Greek or Hebrew, parsed and explained, with every form and cross-reference verified before it's written.
  8. 8
    FormationPick one concrete practice — not all of them.
  9. 9
    Response / PrayerA prayer that grows directly out of the passage, not a generic close.
  10. 10
    One Thing to Carry TodayThe single sentence to leave with.

Why AuDHD-aware?

Scripture doesn't need to be simplified for an AuDHD mind — it needs to be shown clearly enough that pattern-seeking, detail-oriented minds can get an actual handhold on it. Every study here verifies its Greek and Hebrew before it's written, flags genuine scholarly debates instead of quietly resolving them, and keeps its neuroplasticity language modest and text-grounded. Nothing here is inferred or assumed.
